physical_mismatches.reason: Studio models a simple 2D steady-state placement. The paper's HotSpot and fast thermal model describe a 2.5D chiplet-on-interposer stack with package layers, and the packet gives no interposer, TIM, heat spreader or heat sink parameters. A 2D representation omits vertical stack and interposer lateral spreading effects.

Cooling and boundary conditions (heat sink, convection, ambient temperature) are not published in the packet. The paper's 77.12 C therefore cannot be reproduced or numerically compared to Studio results.

The final RLPlanner placement coordinates for the Ascend 910 are not published, so x_m and y_m of each chiplet are unknown. Any Studio placement would be a separate illustrative layout, not the paper's floorplan.

The paper's temperature comes from RL-optimized placement co-optimized with wirelength and a temperature-limit reward. The fast thermal model has about 0.25 K MAE relative to HotSpot, and it is unclear which solver produced the Table I temperatures. Studio's solver differs from both.

The paper has no transient behavior or time-series power. The one-row static power trace is consistent with the steady-state paper observable, but there is no controller or reliability analysis to compare.
Final chiplet coordinates are not supplied by the reference files; generated shelf positions illustrate a 2D power snapshot, not the published placement.

studio_assumptions: Any Studio run would use a separately constructed illustrative 2D placement, with generated coordinates kept distinct from paper-derived facts.
Powers would be a one-row static trace from the pinned Ascend910.cfg: 256, 14, 20, 20, 20, 20 W.

Chiplet dimensions would come from the pinned config, converted from mm to m (conversion factor 0.001): widths 14.5, 10.5, 7.75, 7.75, 7.75, 7.75 mm and heights 31.4, 16, 11.87, 11.87, 11.87, 11.87 mm.

Chiplet names are not given in the config, so generic indexed names would be used, with the order assumed to match the config lists. Which chiplet is the 256 W compute die is inferred from the largest power and size, not stated.
Studio's own package, material and cooling assumptions apply and are not specified in the packet. Studio temperatures are not numerically compared to the paper's 77.12 C.
RLPlanner publishes Ascend910 chiplet sizes and powers, but this config has no placement, power time series, or HotSpot configuration.
The power trace is one constant row made from source per-chiplet watts.
